items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: And this is what Howard did in the Gil Evans orchestra when he was working for Gil Evans. Because I actually played trombone with Howard sitting next to me.

ctx.x: Yeah most definitely. So again, like mentors and stuff, people that you run into that change your life and change your course in history. So in New York City like I said, I grew up on the Latin, you know, New York scene, on the lower east side, which was a big Latin mecca. So I was playing — I had a valve trombone that I was doing gigs on on the Latin scene, playing valve trombones. And during the weekend the Latin scene, you can do a gig, an early gig starting around maybe eight, then you move to another venue…

interesting things on the tuba. So he came in and he just like shattered my thoughts of what a tuba can do in a improvisational setting, or a setting where the music is not written down or structured and everything. Where I’m not playing a tuba part but I’m actually doing what the saxophones and everybody else is doing. I’m given the freedom to improvise and do all types of things. So Howard kind of reset my mind, and then I was also able to join his group at that time it was called Substructure. It was a group…
